entry.title: Sapphire 2026 Key Take Aways for Data Leaders - What did you take away?
entry.content:
Here are some of the take-aways from SAP Sapphire Madrid in May 2026, for us data professionals who are keen to learn more about how SAP is elevating data to its strategic pinnacle.  

We’ve always known the importance of data so it was rewarding to hear the same impressions from the SAP leadership.  The Business Data Cloud (BDC) featured prominently in the keynotes, showcasing its evolution into a robust, integrated business data fabric that enables the business value with contextual SAP and non-SAP data. . Announcements highlighted significant advancements in BDC’s semantic layer, promising unprecedented data quality and harmonization across diverse data sources – a critical enabler for reliable analytics and AI. We saw concrete examples of BDC streamlining data management and enhancing data governance, underpinning compliance and trusted decision-making, which is paramount for data leaders. During my Data Products presentation I highlighted the soon to be generally available Data Product Studio, a BDC toolset that expands data product search, enables the creation of custom data products and data product management.  An exciting development is the use of AI agents to automate many of the data product management tasks, starting with data product creation.

Strategic partnerships were a major focal point at the Sapphire Madrid event.. SAP revealed expanded collaborations with leading hyperscalers, ensuring seamless, scalable data ingestion and secure infrastructure for advanced generative AI model training. Furthermore, new alliances with specialized AI firms were announced, designed to embed sophisticated, industry-specific AI capabilities directly into SAP applications, augmenting offerings like Joule. This emphasis on unified, governed data through BDC, coupled with a robust partner ecosystem for AI innovation, marks an exciting, data-driven future for the intelligent enterprise, grounded in trust and accessibility.  As SAP expands its hyperscaler collaboration model it’s great to see announcements that truly underscored SAP’s commitment to flexibility, scale and leveraging best of breed infrastructure for its data and AI strategy.  It wasn’t just about presence but deeper, more integrated capabilities with Google Cloud Platform, Amazon Web Services and Microsoft Azure.

 The announcement of the Dremio and Reltio acquisitions, finalized shortly before Sapphire, brought cutting-edge data virtualization and semantic modeling platforms into the SAP fold. For a global data executive, this is crucial because it promises to accelerate the realization of a true business data fabric. It means we can logically integrate data from disparate sources – SAP and non-SAP, on-premise and cloud – without costly physical replication. These acquisitions will give our customers a governed, context-rich foundation for agentic AI, analytics, and business applications. Specifically, these new capabilities, aligned with the Business Data Cloud will significantly improve data lineage, ensure consistent data definitions across the enterprise, and provide a unified, trusted view of information critical for advanced analytics and AI, directly enhancing BDC’s capabilities and easing compliance burdens.

So, it was certainly refreshing to see data and AI take center stage at Sapphire and I’m confident that over the next quarters/before the end of 2026 we will see even more capabilities that enable SAP’s data and AI strategy: the release of new assistants and agents, more strategic partnerships and further evidence of SAP’s open data source approach. 

What were your key Sapphire moments and takeaways as a Data Professional?

entry.title: Project Cost Line Items – Loss of Cumulative and Commitment-Based Measures in Recent Releases
entry.content:
Project Cost Line Items – Loss of Cumulative and Commitment-Based Measures in Recent Releases

I would like to raise a concern regarding the evolution of the Project Cost Line Items application.

In older S/4HANA releases, the application F2538 – Project Cost Line Items provided several analytical measures that were extremely useful for project controlling and cost analysis.

Reference:

  • SAP Help document 

  • SAP Fiori App Library: F2538

As shown in SAP documentation and screenshots from earlier releases, users could analyze project costs using measures such as:

  • Cumulative Actual Cost

  • Cumulative Planned Cost

  • Cumulative Actual Cost + Commitments

  • Commitment values originating from open Purchase Requisitions and Purchase Orders

These measures enabled the creation of trend analyses and S-curves, allowing project managers to compare:

  • Planned vs. Actual evolution over time

  • Actual + Commitment evolution over time

  • Cost performance by fiscal period and fiscal year using cumulative values

The chart below illustrates the type of cumulative analysis that was possible in previous releases, where values evolved period after period rather than being displayed as isolated figures.

 

Since S/4HANA 2023, the application has been replaced by F6992 – Project Costs – Line Items.

Reference:

  • SAP Help document 

  • SAP Fiori App Library: F6992

However, the newer application appears to have lost several important analytical capabilities.

The cumulative measures mentioned above are no longer available, and commitment-related measures seem to have been removed as well. As a result:

  • Users can only analyze values for individual periods.

  • Cumulative cost evolution cannot be displayed.

  • Actual Cost + Commitments analysis is no longer possible.

  • Commitment visibility (open Purchase Requisitions and Purchase Orders) is missing.

  • Building project cost S-curves directly from the standard application is no longer feasible.

From a project controlling perspective, this feels like a regression in reporting capabilities rather than an enhancement.

Has anyone found an alternative standard application that provides the same cumulative and commitment-based analysis?

Is there any roadmap item, SAP Note, or Customer Influence request addressing the reintroduction of these measures in F6992?

I would be interested in understanding how other customers and consultants are handling this limitation in S/4HANA 2023 and 2025.

Regards
Marcio Blos

entry.title: SAP Analytics Cloud+JVA: Unable to Retrieve Cash Call Data from Released CDS Views
entry.content:
I am developing a Joint Venture (JV) cash call report for an upstream oil and gas company. The client is running SAP S/4HANA Public Cloud with Joint Venture Accounting (JVA) and SAP Analytics Cloud (SAC), integrated through both live and import connections.

Using the live connection, I explored the following released CDS views:

  • 2CCPVJVACCTGDTLQRY – JV Accounting Detail Query
  • 2CCPVJVADTLHIERQRY – JV Accounting Detail Hierarchy Query

However, both CDS views return no data even after providing the required query parameters, despite JVA transactions existing in the system. I am therefore trying to determine whether this behavior is due to configuration, authorizations, a product limitation or whether these CDS views are not intended to expose cash call transactions for this business scenario.

To further investigate, we established an import connection to SAP S/4HANA and exposed the A_JournalEntryLineItem CDS view to determine whether it contains the required data for the report. After importing the data into SAC, we analyzed the dataset using the SAC explorer tool. A preview of the imported data is attached.

Our objective is to build a report that captures cash call payments received from non-operating partners. However, the A_JournalEntryLineItem dataset contains a broad range of financial postings, including WBS - related and other unrelated transactions, making it difficult to isolate the relevant cash call entries.

I would appreciate guidance on the following:

  1. Why do the JVA CDS views return no data despite JVA transactions existing in the system?
  2. Are there any prerequisite configuration steps, communication arrangements or authorizations required for these CDS views to return data?
  3. Which dimensions or fields, filters or business logic should be applied to the A_JournalEntryLineItem dataset to isolate cash call transactions from non-operating partners?
  4. Is there a specific indicator, document type, business transaction or JVA-related field that uniquely identifies cash call payments?
  5. If A_JournalEntryLineItem is not the recommended data source, is there another released CDS view or API that should be used to report on cash call transactions in SAP S/4HANA Public Cloud with JVA?

Any guidance or recommendations would be greatly appreciated. Thank you.

SAP Analytics Cloud, connectivity SAP Joint Venture Accounting SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition

entry.title: Custom CDS view missing in SAP Analytics Cloud (SAC) - SAP S/4HANA PCE
entry.content:
I am working on exposing a custom CDS view created in SAP S/4HANA Public Cloud so that it can be consumed through a live connection in SAP Analytics Cloud (SAC). However, the custom analytical query is not appearing in the list of available queries.

Below are the steps I followed to create the query:

  1. In the Custom CDS Views app, I created a custom CDS view using the Analytical Cube scenario.
  2. In the Custom Analytical Queries and Services app, I created the analytical query and published it. On the General tab, I selected the Expose as OData V2 option. See the attached screenshots.

Note: The Custom Analytical Queries app no longer supports query creation.

       3. In the View Browser app, I searched for the analytical query and clicked Create Application to generate the Application ID. See the attached screenshot.

       4. In the Custom Catalog Extensions app, I filtered the list using the IAM Application ID and added the following business catalogs, along with their required dependencies:

  • Analytics – Analytical Query Application Design (ID: SAP_CORE_BC_EXT_AQA_PC)
  • Foundation – Extensibility Explorer Apps (ID: SAP_CA_BC_EXT_COCKPIT_PC)
  • Analytics – Query Design (ID: SAP_BW_BC_AQD_PC)
  • Analytics – Review Booklet Design (ID: SAP_CORE_BC_EXT_RVB_PC)

In the SAC Modeler, I am creating a Live Data Model and using SAP BW as the system type.

Despite completing these steps, the custom analytical query does not appear in the list of available queries. I have searched using technical name with both the 2C or 2CZ prefixes but the query still does not appear.

Has anyone encountered this issue before or are there additional configuration steps or prerequisites that I may have missed? Any guidance or recommendations would be greatly appreciated.  Thank you.

entry.title: G/L Account Logic vs Semantic Tags for Finance Reporting
entry.content:
Hi all,

I'm currently working on a BW to SAP Datasphere migration and came across an architectural question while translating existing Finance reporting logic.

In BW, reporting logic often directly references G/L accounts or groups of G/L accounts. When rebuilding this logic in Datasphere, would it be better to continue with the same approach, or would it be more sustainable to maintain semantic tags for G/L accounts and build the reporting logic around those semantic classifications?

For example, instead of repeatedly maintaining logic such as:

G/L Account IN (Account 1, Account 2, Account 3...)

The logic could potentially be based on a semantic classification:

Semantic Tag = COGS

The challenge is that semantic tags require proper maintenance and governance as the chart of accounts evolves. This introduces an additional maintenance activity, particularly when new G/L accounts are created or existing accounts change classification.

However, once the semantic classification is maintained, the same logic could potentially be reused across multiple Datasphere models, KPIs, and Analytics use cases without repeatedly maintaining G/L account lists.

So my question is:

For a BW to Datasphere migration, which approach is more sustainable for a long-term Finance and Analytics landscape?

  • Replicate the existing BW approach using G/L account-based logic
  • Invest in semantic-tag maintenance and use semantic classifications for reusable Finance logic
  • Use a hybrid approach, where semantic tags are used for common Finance classifications and G/L-based logic is retained for more specific reporting requirements

I'd be particularly interested in hearing from those who have implemented semantic tags in Datasphere at scale.

Thanks in advance!

entry.title: RAW → Harmonization → Reporting: Where should Business Logic live?
entry.content:
A common approach is:
RAW → HARMONIZATION → REPORTING → SAC

On paper, this separation looks straightforward. But in real implementation projects, the boundaries between these layers can become less obvious.

One question I’ve been thinking about while working with SAP Datasphere: Where should business logic actually live in Raw, Harmonization, or Reporting?

For example:
COGS should be calculated from specific GL accounts, with sign inversion and certain account mappings applied.

Would you typically implement that logic in the HARMONIZATION layer, so it becomes reusable across multiple reports?

Or would you keep harmonization closer to the source data and implement the business rule in the REPORTING/Analytical Model layer, where it is directly tied to the reporting requirement?

I'm particularly interested in real project experience here.

Have you encountered cases where putting business logic in the wrong layer caused problems later, such as duplicated logic, inconsistent KPIs, performance issues, or having to redesign the model close to go-live?

Are there any Datasphere-specific limitations or best practices that influence where you place this logic?

Would love to hear how others approach this in actual implementations.

Thanks.
